objective: Maintain a longitudinal, configuration-specific record of X1 inspection, wear, service, contamination, impact, and future telemetry-triggered findings without allowing maintenance state to substitute for build or operating authority.

health_states.meaning: No unresolved inspect/service/stop findings are present and the latest applicable preflight is complete.
At least one unresolved condition requires inspection before the next activity.
At least one unresolved condition requires corrective service before the next activity.
At least one unresolved stop-use finding exists; no further ride/test activity should proceed until repaired and explicitly closed.

automatic_event_escalations.rationale: Movement at a critical retention joint requires mechanism investigation before continued use.
Wheel retention uncertainty can cause sudden component separation.
Structural damage requires explicit inspection/repair before reuse.
Independent friction braking is a hard system requirement.
Steering interference can cause loss of control.
Ingress requires drying, inspection, and root-cause correction before continued use.
Abrasion can progress into electrical or brake failure.
Bearing condition change should be inspected before the next allowed activity.
Pressure loss can indicate puncture, valve, tube, bead, or measurement problems.
Impact can create hidden retention, alignment, or structural damage.

service_interval_policy.rule: Do not invent mileage, hour, calendar, torque, replacement, or lubrication intervals before the selected component manufacturer or a later qualified X1 physical program provides them.
service_interval_policy.due_rule: When multiple sourced limits exist, the earliest applicable condition wins. Event/condition findings can require service sooner than any interval.
service_interval_policy.reset_rule: A service action may reset an interval only when the component has a declared sourced interval and the action records a nonempty source_reference.

chronology_rules: exactly one BASELINE event is allowed and it must be the first health event
event timestamps must be unique after normalization to UTC
active components cannot appear in events before their installation timestamp
ride hours cannot decrease when present
component IDs referenced by events must exist in the current registry or be introduced by the same configuration-change event
configuration changes must be explicit rather than silently rewriting history

privacy_and_storage.public_repository: schemas, tools, reference rules, synthetic tests
privacy_and_storage.private_workspace: board identifiers, serials, exact ride history, maintenance notes, measurements, photos and future telemetry

hard_boundaries: health state never authorizes powered operation
health state never authorizes public operation
health state never authorizes dog-accompanied operation
health state never overrides a blocked build-authority gate
READY_FOR_ALLOWED_ACTIVITY means ready only for an activity independently permitted elsewhere
missing required preflight checks cannot produce READY_FOR_ALLOWED_ACTIVITY
open STOP findings cannot be downgraded by a later preflight without an explicit closure/service event
manufacturer service requirements cannot be weakened by this project
READY state requires exactly one first-event BASELINE plus a fresh current-configuration PREFLIGHT
lifecycle health evidence must link to the exact rolling-chassis authority fingerprint used by the central build graph
